meta_description: Conversational triage with safety gates — 74% of intake conversations resolved without clinician time and escalation accuracy independently audited at 96%

blocks.x: Conversational triage with safety gates — 74% of intake conversations resolved without clinician time and escalation accuracy independently audited at 96%
a telehealth provider whose nurses spent half their shifts asking the questions a good intake form should have asked. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline week measured the shifts: 52% of clinician time on intake that followed deterministic patterns, and the previous chatbot retired after it once reassured a patient whose symptoms merited an urgent pathway.
Safety was the whole product. Any automation that could not prove its escalation behavior was worse than the queue it relieved.

We built triage as a conversation with gates: red-flag detection runs on every turn outside the language model, urgent pathways are hard-routed with no model discretion, and the escalation behavior was audited against a clinician-labeled historical cohort before any patient saw it. Nurses enter conversations already carrying the structured intake summary.
